name: Hudson River Estuary Grants: Local Stewardship Planning

funder.name: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

summary: Hudson River Estuary grants for local stewardship planning, climate adaptation, habitat conservation planning and tributary watershed stewardship in the estuary watershed.
reporting: Quarterly progress and financial reports are required for Hudson River Estuary Program grants.

eligibility.rule: Registered in the NYS Grants Management system
A nonprofit applicant is prequalified in SFS Grants Management by the bid due date
Not-for-profits are incorporated in New York and current in charities reporting to the Attorney General

documents: Letters of collaboration from all partners naming the lead, if applicable
Gender-Based Violence and the Workplace certification (Attachment G)
Match Worksheet listing all match sources

status.quote: Grant funding is currently available for municipalities and non-profit organizations within the Hudson River Estuary Program boundaries

deadline.quote: Applications are due in the State Financial System (SFS) at 3 p.m. on December 17, 2026.

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include Governmental Entities, Municipalities, and Quasi-Governmental Entities, including but not limited to Counties, Cities, Towns, Villages, or Indian nation or tribe

geography.quote: Grant funding is currently available for municipalities and non-profit organizations within the Hudson River Estuary Program boundaries

access.quote: Applications are due in the State Financial System (SFS) at 3 p.m. on December 17, 2026.

window.quote: Four Requests for Applications (RFAs) are available: Tributary Restoration and Resilience, Local Stewardship Planning, River Education, and River Access.

amount.quote: The minimum grant award for Local Stewardship Planning is $10,500 and the maximum is $50,000.

pool.quote: $350,000 for Local Stewardship Planning Approximately $350,000 is available

reporting.quote: Reporting is required on a quarterly basis for all Hudson River Estuary Program grants.

eligibility.quote: must be registered in the NYS Grants Management system to be eligible to apply for any NYS grant opportunity.
A not-for-profit organization must also be prequalified in SFS Grants Management by the bid due date to be determined eligible under this grant opportunity.
has filed a Certificate of Incorporation to be incorporated in New York State and is current in their charities reporting requirements with the Office of the Attorney General.

documents.quote: The bidder must provide a map of the site, uploaded to SFS Grants Management.
Bidders MUST provide a timeline for meeting project objectives and identified tasks between August 1, 2027 and July 31, 2030.
This worksheet is required to be uploaded in SFS Grants Management for all applications.
If applicable, letters of collaboration are provided from all Bidder partners, which must include “Lead” Bidder designation.

The Bidder must provide the required certification for sexual harassment prevention ("Attachment S"), as required by State Finance Law §139-l. The Bidder must provide the required EO 16 Certification. The Bidder must provide the required Gender-Based Violence and the Workplace Certification ("Attachment G") as required by State Finance Law §139-m.
Bidders will be required to provide the sources of all matching funds using the Match Worksheet in SFS Grants Management.
This Bid Checklist is completed and uploaded.

co_finance_required.quote: For this grant opportunity, Bidders must match at least 15% of the grant funding amount.

after_award.quote: Quarterly Narrative Reports must be submitted in narrative form, no later than 30 days from the end of the calendar quarter.
